Player forecasts are well calibrated. On the holdout, predicted buckets landed within about 3 points of actual hit rates. The test used who actually played, so live forecasts will be slightly worse because inactives are unknown in advance.

Game lines show no edge. Closing spread MAE was 9.70 points vs 10.11 for our line, and the fitted weight on our line was about zero. Closing totals: 10.18 vs 10.61. So game sides default to pass.

Prop edges are unproven. Calibration shows the probabilities are honest. It does not show they beat DraftKings, because no historical prop lines were available to test against. The edges here are leads to price-check.

2026 holdout, all markets. Dots near the dashed line mean a forecast of X% hit about X% of the time. Bigger dots hold more forecasts.

Data gaps

  • Prop prices: ESPN's DraftKings feed gives lines and milestone levels but no prices. Moneyline, spread and total prices are real. Prop edges assume -110, and each pick shows a minimum acceptable price.
  • 2026 coverage: man/zone and coverage shells have no free 2026 feed. 2025 charting stands in, labeled every time, and flagged when a head coach changed. Coordinator changes are not tracked.
  • Alignment and routes: 2026 slot/wide alignment and routes run are paid data. Target side, depth and 2025 route targets stand in. Press rate, shadow rate, tackle-vs-edge win rate, and run-scheme splits are left out.
  • Under-pressure splits: team pressure rates are 2026 (PFR). Individual QB pressure splits are 2025. Blitz splits are 2026 (FTN).
  • Injury odds: P(plays) values are assumptions from status and practice, not fitted estimates.

nflverse supplied play-by-play, FTN charting, PFR advanced stats, NGS, snap counts, depth charts and rosters. ESPN supplied the schedule, injuries and DraftKings lines. NWS supplied forecasts.

These are estimates, and no selection is guaranteed. After the games, run review.py to score every forecast (Phase 15).

BUF defense vs MIA offense: what to attack

  • BUF is soft on Inter 10-19 throws to the right (+0.47 EPA/att vs league +0.29, 34 attempts).
  • Avoid Deep 20+ throws to the left: BUF allows -0.22 EPA/att vs league +0.30 (12 attempts).
  • Pressure mismatch favors BUF: its 26% pressure rate meets a MIA line allowing 26% (league 22%).
  • Run stuffed: Outside (tackle / end) gains only 3.9 YPC on BUF (league 4.5).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Caleb Douglas (WR, Questionable), Dante Trader Jr. (S, Doubtful), Chris Bell (WR, Questionable), Andrew Meyer (C, Questionable), Christian Benford (CB, Questionable), Dee Alford (CB, Questionable), Ray Davis (RB, Questionable), T.J. Sanders (DT, Questionable), Dalton Kincaid (TE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Kyle McCord and Josh Allen. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: DJ Moore 10+ receiving yds (90%) + Josh Allen 150+ passing yds (89%). Joint estimate 83.0%, fair -487. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 74.6% vs 71.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: DJ Moore 20+ receiving yds (80%) + Khalil Shakir 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Josh Allen 180+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 59.2%, fair -145. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.2% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Allen 220+ passing yds (61%) + DJ Moore 40+ receiving yds (59%) + James Cook 80+ rushing yds (59%). Joint estimate 28.7%, fair +248. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.1% vs 14.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: DJ Moore 10+ receiving yds (90%) + Josh Allen 150+ passing yds (89%). Joint estimate 83.0%, fair -487. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 74.6% vs 71.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: DJ Moore 20+ receiving yds (80%) + Khalil Shakir 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Josh Allen 180+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 59.2%, fair -145. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.2% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Allen 220+ passing yds (61%) + DJ Moore 40+ receiving yds (59%) + James Cook 80+ rushing yds (59%). Joint estimate 28.7%, fair +248. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.1% vs 14.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Erik McCoy (C, Doubtful), Taliese Fuaga (OT, Doubtful), Jordyn Tyson (WR, Questionable), Martin Emerson Jr. (CB, Questionable), Pete Werner (LB, Questionable), Kyler Gordon (CB, Questionable), Jeffery Simmons (DT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Tyler Shough and Caleb Williams. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Caleb Williams 160+ passing yds (93%) + Rome Odunze 10+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 87.8%, fair -717. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.0% vs 79.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Chris Olave 30+ receiving yds (78%) + Caleb Williams 210+ passing yds (77%) + Tyler Shough 180+ passing yds (77%). Joint estimate 53.8%, fair -117. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.0% vs 35.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Kyle Monangai 30+ rushing yds (61%) + Tyler Shough 210+ passing yds (60%) + Caleb Williams 247+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 24.2%, fair +313. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.8% vs 16.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Tyjae Spears (RB, Questionable), Carnell Tate (WR, Questionable), Kevin Winston Jr. (S, Questionable), Cody Barton (LB, Questionable), Anthony Hill Jr. (LB, Questionable), Donovan Ezeiruaku (LB, Questionable), Shavon Revel Jr. (CB, Questionable), Luke Schoonmaker (TE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Cam Ward and Dak Prescott. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Dak Prescott 190+ passing yds (93%) + George Pickens 20+ receiving yds (93%). Joint estimate 88.7%, fair -788. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 82.3% vs 80.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: CeeDee Lamb 60+ receiving yds (79%) + Cam Ward 180+ passing yds (78%) + Ryan Flournoy 15+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 48.3%, fair +107. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 38.0% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tony Pollard 50+ rushing yds (62%) + Cam Ward 210+ passing yds (61%) + Dak Prescott 290+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 25.1%, fair +298. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.5% vs 16.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Dak Prescott 190+ passing yds (93%) + George Pickens 20+ receiving yds (93%). Joint estimate 88.7%, fair -788. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 82.3% vs 80.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: CeeDee Lamb 60+ receiving yds (79%) + Cam Ward 180+ passing yds (78%) + Ryan Flournoy 15+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 48.3%, fair +107. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 38.0% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tony Pollard 50+ rushing yds (62%) + Cam Ward 210+ passing yds (61%) + Dak Prescott 290+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 25.1%, fair +298. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.5% vs 16.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Baker Mayfield (QB, Questionable), Antoine Winfield Jr. (S, Questionable), Yaya Diaby (LB, Questionable), Sione Vaki (RB, Questionable), D.J. Reed (CB, Questionable), Tyler Lacy (DT, Questionable), Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Baker Mayfield and Jared Goff. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Emeka Egbuka 10+ receiving yds (91%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 40+ rushing yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.7%, fair -513. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.7% vs 77.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Emeka Egbuka 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Bucky Irving 40+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.4%, fair +107. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.2% vs 35.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jared Goff 230+ passing yds (62%) + Sam LaPorta 30+ receiving yds (61%) + Jameson Williams 40+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 33.6%, fair +198. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.8% vs 14.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Emeka Egbuka 10+ receiving yds (91%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 40+ rushing yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.7%, fair -513. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.7% vs 77.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Emeka Egbuka 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Bucky Irving 40+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.4%, fair +107. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.2% vs 35.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jared Goff 230+ passing yds (62%) + Sam LaPorta 30+ receiving yds (61%) + Jameson Williams 40+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 33.6%, fair +198. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.8% vs 14.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Hjalte Froholdt (C, Questionable), Carson Beck (QB, Questionable), Roy Lopez (DT, Questionable), Kenneth Walker III (RB, Questionable), Omarr Norman-Lott (DT, Questionable), Trey Smith (G, Questionable), Jaylon Moore (OT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Carson Beck and Patrick Mahomes. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Trey McBride 20+ receiving yds (92%) + Rashee Rice 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.0%, fair -487. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 74.9% vs 74.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Patrick Mahomes 190+ passing yds (80%) + Xavier Worthy 10+ receiving yds (77%) + Rashee Rice 25+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 53.6%, fair -116. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.0% vs 33.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Downs 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Xavier Worthy 20+ receiving yds (59%) + Rashee Rice 40+ receiving yds (58%). Joint estimate 20.6%, fair +385. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 11.4% vs 11.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Trey McBride 20+ receiving yds (92%) + Rashee Rice 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.0%, fair -487. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 74.9% vs 74.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Patrick Mahomes 190+ passing yds (80%) + Xavier Worthy 10+ receiving yds (77%) + Rashee Rice 25+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 53.6%, fair -116. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.0% vs 33.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Downs 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Xavier Worthy 20+ receiving yds (59%) + Rashee Rice 40+ receiving yds (58%). Joint estimate 20.6%, fair +385. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 11.4% vs 11.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Nick Herbig (LB, Questionable), Smael Mondon Jr. (LB, Questionable), Dontayvion Wicks (WR, Questionable), Nolan Smith Jr. (LB, Questionable), Zack Baun (LB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Aaron Rodgers and Joe Milton III. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: DK Metcalf 10+ receiving yds (92%) + Aaron Rodgers 150+ passing yds (81%). Joint estimate 77.8%, fair -350. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 69.3% vs 66.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dallas Goedert 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Joe Milton III 150+ passing yds (77%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (76%). Joint estimate 49.8%, fair +101. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 36.3% vs 33.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Pat Freiermuth 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Darnell Washington 15+ receiving yds (60%) + Joe Milton III 180+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 22.5%, fair +344. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.5% vs 16.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: DK Metcalf 10+ receiving yds (92%) + Aaron Rodgers 150+ passing yds (81%). Joint estimate 77.8%, fair -350. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 69.3% vs 66.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dallas Goedert 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Joe Milton III 150+ passing yds (77%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (76%). Joint estimate 49.8%, fair +101. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 36.3% vs 33.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Pat Freiermuth 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Darnell Washington 15+ receiving yds (60%) + Joe Milton III 180+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 22.5%, fair +344. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.5% vs 16.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Nnamdi Madubuike (DT, Questionable), Jaylinn Hawkins (S, Questionable), Adisa Isaac (LB, Questionable), Tommy Tremble (TE, Questionable), Darren Waller (TE, Questionable), Bobby Okereke (LB, Questionable), Isaiah Simmons (S, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Jacoby Brissett and Bryce Young. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Chuba Hubbard 30+ rushing yds (91%) + Tetairoa McMillan 15+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 82.6%, fair -475. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.3% vs 76.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Jalen Coker 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Mark Andrews 10+ receiving yds (79%) + Tetairoa McMillan 30+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 48.2%, fair +107. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 34.2% vs 33.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Derrick Henry 50+ rushing yds (60%) + Bryce Young 220+ passing yds (60%) + Chuba Hubbard 60+ rushing yds (60%). Joint estimate 21.6%, fair +362. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 15.7% vs 15.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Geno Smith (QB, Questionable), Harrison Phillips (DT, Questionable), Joseph Ossai (DE, Questionable), Charlie Kolar (TE, Questionable), Ladd McConkey (WR, Questionable), Daiyan Henley (LB, Questionable), Donte Jackson (CB, Questionable), Kendall Williamson (S, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Geno Smith and Justin Herbert. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Garrett Wilson 20+ receiving yds (92%) + Braelon Allen 15+ rushing yds (90%). Joint estimate 83.0%, fair -488. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.9% vs 76.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Justin Herbert 150+ passing yds (80%) + Breece Hall 20+ rushing yds (79%) + Adonai Mitchell 20+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 50.0%, fair -100. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 39.1% vs 38.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Breece Hall 30+ rushing yds (62%) + Mason Taylor 15+ receiving yds (59%) + Braelon Allen 40+ rushing yds (57%). Joint estimate 21.5%, fair +365. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 16.0% vs 15.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Trey Zuhn III (C, Questionable), Ian Thomas (TE, Questionable), Brock Bowers (TE, Questionable), Tonka Hemingway (DT, Questionable), Folorunso Fatukasi (DT, Questionable), Jaylen Waddle (WR, Questionable), Riley Moss (CB, Questionable), Brandon Jones (S, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Fernando Mendoza and Bo Nix. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Fernando Mendoza 150+ passing yds (85%) + Courtland Sutton 10+ receiving yds (85%). Joint estimate 73.1%, fair -271. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 63.5% vs 63.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Bo Nix 160+ passing yds (79%) + Courtland Sutton 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Ashton Jeanty 15+ rushing yds (77%). Joint estimate 50.9%, fair -104. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.4% vs 36.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Pat Bryant 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Evan Engram 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Bo Nix 200+ passing yds (59%). Joint estimate 28.8%, fair +247. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 22.5% vs 17.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Fernando Mendoza 150+ passing yds (85%) + Courtland Sutton 10+ receiving yds (85%). Joint estimate 73.1%, fair -271. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 63.5% vs 63.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Bo Nix 160+ passing yds (79%) + Courtland Sutton 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Ashton Jeanty 15+ rushing yds (77%). Joint estimate 50.9%, fair -104. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.4% vs 36.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Pat Bryant 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Evan Engram 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Bo Nix 200+ passing yds (59%). Joint estimate 28.8%, fair +247. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 22.5% vs 17.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Bhayshul Tuten (RB, Questionable), LeQuint Allen Jr. (RB, Questionable), Chris Rodriguez Jr. (RB, Questionable), Jakobi Meyers (WR, Questionable), Danny Striggow (DE, Questionable), Nic Jones (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Trevor Lawrence and J.J. McCarthy. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Malik Nabers 15+ receiving yds (94%) + Parker Washington 15+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 85.2%, fair -577. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.9% vs 77.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Isaiah Likely 25+ receiving yds (79%) + J.J. McCarthy 180+ passing yds (78%) + Trevor Lawrence 190+ passing yds (76%). Joint estimate 52.9%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.5% vs 35.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Trevor Lawrence 220+ passing yds (62%) + Malik Nabers 50+ receiving yds (61%) + Theo Johnson 8+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 24.4%, fair +310. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.0% vs 15.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Blake Cashman (LB, Questionable), Isaiah Rodgers (CB, Questionable), T.J. Hockenson (TE, Questionable), Andrew Van Ginkel (LB, Questionable), Dre Greenlaw (LB, Questionable), Mac Jones (QB, Questionable), Jordan James (RB, Questionable), Mike Evans (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Christian McCaffrey 15+ rushing yds (91%) + George Kittle 10+ receiving yds (88%). Joint estimate 79.6%, fair -389. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 72.2% vs 72.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Brock Purdy 180+ passing yds (79%) + Aaron Jones 20+ rushing yds (79%) + Christian McCaffrey 25+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.9%, fair +105. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 40.1% vs 40.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Aaron Jones 31+ rushing yds (61%) + George Kittle 30+ receiving yds (61%) + Brock Purdy 220+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 27.0%, fair +271. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.1% vs 14.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative: Christian McCaffrey 15+ rushing yds (91%) + George Kittle 10+ receiving yds (88%). Joint estimate 79.6%, fair -389. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 72.2% vs 72.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Brock Purdy 180+ passing yds (79%) + Aaron Jones 20+ rushing yds (79%) + Christian McCaffrey 25+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.9%, fair +105. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 40.1% vs 40.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Aaron Jones 31+ rushing yds (61%) + George Kittle 30+ receiving yds (61%) + Brock Purdy 220+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 27.0%, fair +271. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.1% vs 14.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.
